verdict.reasoning: Patient reports a “blinding headache for a few days” and says it makes it “very hard to focus” and that she “can't even go to work.” Duration elsewhere clarified as three days: “that was three days ago, and I just keep having it.”

Onset: “it just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago.” Location: “it's kind of all over but, I feel like over my right eye, it's... stronger,” consistent with right supraorbital > holocephalic and constant: “kinda all the time.”

Severity: “I guess it's mostly, eight, and then it kinda comes down to maybe a five.” Effect of ibuprofen: “Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen either… It gets a little bit better but like, doesn't go away.”

Photophobia: “lights definitely make me more sensitive. Like, um, I don't really, like strong lights.” Visual disturbance: “I think, I get this, shooting light sometimes… just a bit of um, weird kind of vision.”
Nausea/vomiting: “Uh, no, feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting.” Neuro symptoms: “Any tingling? Or numbness? Or weakness anywhere?” Patient: “Um, no.”

Fever: Doctor notes “you haven't had a high temperature. Have you checked your temperature?” Patient: “Uh, no I didn't, I don't really feel, feverish or anything.” No URI/sinus/cough: “have you had any cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears, or pain over the sinuses? Any cough or flem?” Patient: “No, no.” No epistaxis: “Any, any nose bleeds, or coughing up any blood or anything?” Patient: “No.” Weight: “any change in your weight?” Patient: “Um, no change of weight.”

Sleep: “What about at night-time, are you able to fall asleep?” Patient: “Um, yeah, I'm, sleeping well.” No nocturnal awakening: “Is it waking you up in the night-time?” Patient: “No, no, no. But I can wake up with it in the morning.”
Positional/head movement: “Sometimes when I stand up, quickly I get a bit of a, stabbing pain. Um, or if I throw my head like, it I kind of feel like something is moving inside.”
Eye check: “have you had any, uh, eye checks recently?” Patient: “Um, yeah, actually had one recently and, nothing changed my vision.”

Past history: “any other, medical problems in the past?” Patient: “Um, I think I only had a, a pain, um, when I was younger but, no causes found and that went away, but that's, the only thing I know of.” This supports that no ongoing/diagnosed past medical history is reported.

Medication: “Do you take any medications?” Patient: “Um, just the pill.” Later: “And when did you start that?” Patient: “Um, about a year ago.” Combined oral contraceptive is implied by later discussion of pill and migraine/aura contraindication.

Ibuprofen use: “I recently had a, a one for like two days, um, but it just went away with Ibuprofen” and “Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen either… I try that,” and later, “apart from the Ibuprofen that I take, sometimes when, the headache gets really bad, nothing else.”
Paracetamol advice: “I can prescribe you something, similar to Ibuprofen, but a bit stronger… And you can also take Paracetamol at the same time.”
Allergies: “Um, and any allergies to anything?” Patient: “No.”
Family history: “my mum, suffers from, like she has migraines… I know that my mum like, she has quite bad migraines, she's like, has the vomiting and everything.”
Living situation: “Who do you live with at home?” Patient: “Uh, just by myself.” Work: “Have you been at work recently?” Patient: “Um, I work from home…”

Work missed: “First day I worked from home and then, um, the second I just took the whole day off. And, today I just tried to work from home the first half of the day but… stopped in the morning.” This supports that at least one full day of work was missed.
Smoking: “And do you smoke?” Patient: “Uh, no.”

Alcohol: “Do you drink any alcohol regularly?” Patient: “Yeah.” “How much in a normal week do you think?” Patient: “Um, probably like, three , once a week.” Interpretable as about three drinks once weekly.
Recreational drugs: “And do you take any other drugs at all?” Patient: “Um, no apart from the Ibuprofen… nothing else.”
Travel: “Have you been abroad recently at all?” Patient: “No.”

Doctor’s assessment: “it, it, it could possibly be a migraine type headache.” Headache is severe (8/10), lasted three days, not resolving with ibuprofen. Red-flag symptoms (fever, neuro deficit, vomiting, weight loss, etc.) were specifically denied, so describing as with no red flags is consistent with the transcript.

Contraindication discussion: “because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights, and things like that.” And: “that pill if you were having, regular migraines with um, flashing lights… It wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill, particularly, we'd have to change it to something else.”

Work and photophobia impact: Patient says she finds it “very hard to focus or, like I can't even go to work” and later explains she missed work days; also notes light sensitivity: “lights definitely make me more sensitive… I don't really, like strong lights.”

In-person exam: “we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination… we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well.” Later: “when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well.” Fundoscopy is implied by “look at the back of your eyes.”

Medication plan: “I can prescribe you something, similar to Ibuprofen, but a bit stronger which you can take instead of Ibuprofen. And you can also take Paracetamol at the same time… take it with food.”
There is no mention of counseling on trigger avoidance, hydration, or resting in a dark, quiet room in the transcript.

Safety netting: “if in the meantime before your appointment your, headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing… then you should go to A and E and have an examination. Um, , you can call us for further advice on that.”
Blood pressure: “when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well.”

Pill change if migraine with aura: “because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights… that pill if you were having, regular migraines with um, flashing lights… It wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill… we'd have to change it to something else.”
There is no discussion of graded return to work or providing a work note in the transcript.
